Stage 02

Statutory Formation & Board Resolutions

Competent registry, governing statute, capital lockup rules, and first board resolution template.

Competent corporate registry

Registro Mercantil Provincial where the registered office is located, coordinated with the Registro Mercantil Central (RMC) for name reservation; electronic filing via the Ventanilla Única Empresarial (VUE) / CIRCE portal.

Governing statute

Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, por el que se aprueba el texto refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (LSC); Articles 20-23 (incorporation formalities), Article 27 (registered office), Articles 102-105 (minimum capital), Articles 209-211 (administrator appointment); supplemented by Real Decreto 1784/1996 (Reglamento del Registro Mercantil).

Formation / constitutional filings

Escritura Pública de Constitución (notarial deed of incorporation) followed by Inscripción en el Registro Mercantil (commercial registration).

Incorporation processing time

⚡ 19 business days (SOP sum)

Paid-up Capital & Blocked Account Regime Mandatory Capital Deposit & Lockup

Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) requires a minimum subscribed and fully paid-up share capital of EUR 3,000 under Article 4 LSC. The full capital must be paid into a bank account opened in the company's name prior to notarization; a bank deposit certificate must be annexed to the deed. No statutory escrow account is mandated, but a notarial deposit or blocked account certification is customary for electronic formation. In-kind contributions require an independent expert valuation report.

Funding & unlock path: Fire safety clearance: premises must comply with Real Decreto 2267/2004 (if industrial/warehouse) or Real Decreto 314/2006 (CTE-DB-SI) for fire-structural behavior. Structural load inspections follow the Código Técnico de la Edificación (CTE-DB-SE). Occupational health and safety clearance requires a risk assessment under Ley 31/1995 and provision of training and emergency measures. Municipal clearance is evidenced through a 'certificado de aptitud' or acknowledgment of the 'comunicación previa' from the local authority.

Paid-in capital rule: Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) requires a minimum subscribed and fully paid-up share capital of EUR 3,000 under Article 4 LSC. The full capital must be paid into a bank account opened in the company's name prior to notarization; a bank deposit certificate must be annexed to the deed. No statutory escrow account is mandated, but a notarial deposit or blocked account certification is customary for electronic formation. In-kind contributions require an independent expert valuation report.

Pro-Forma First Board Resolution Draft
RESOLVED: (1) The founding partners hereby incorporate a private limited liability company (Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada) under the name certified by the Mercantile Registry and adopt the attached bylaws. (2) The entire share capital of EUR 3,000 is subscribed and fully paid in, as evidenced by the bank deposit certificate. (3) The registered office is fixed at Calle de Alcalá 21, 28014 Madrid. (4) [Full Name] is appointed sole administrator for an indefinite term with all powers under the bylaws. (5) The administrator is expressly authorized to sign the public deed, obtain the Tax Identification Number, register with the Mercantile Registry and Social Security, apply for all licenses and permits, and open corporate bank accounts as necessary to perfect the incorporation.
Industrial Access / EIA & Civil Defense Approval Exempted / Not Required

No specific industrial licensing board is applicable for a pure re-invoicing trade (ISIC 4690). If physical premises are established, the competent municipal authority is the Ayuntamiento (for activity license) and the regional Consejería de Medio Ambiente (for any environmental controls).

Category: Not applicable for the re-invoicing hub activity. For any office or warehouse presence, the relevant municipal permit is 'Licencia de Apertura y Funcionamiento' or 'Comunicación Previa' under the Spanish Services Directive.

Stage 03

Tax Identity & Indirect Tax

Tax authority e-portal, entity tax classification elections, VAT thresholds, and 0% export documentation chain.

Tax ID Application Infrastructure

Competent tax authority

Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) - Sede Electrónica at https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es

E-government filing portal

For the Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL), the statutory TIN is the NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal), obtained automatically upon incorporation at the Commercial Registry and verification through the AEAT. For a foreign entity without a permanent establishment in Spain, the procedure is to appoint a fiscal representative (if required), submit Form 036 (Censo de Empresarios/Profesionales) or Form 037, together with a power-of-attorney and identity documents, to the competent AEAT office, following which the entity is assigned a provisional NIF-IVA (VAT registration number) or definitively registered as a taxable person. The application must be made prior to the commencement of any taxable activity in Spain; for EU entities, the NIF-IVA may also be sought through the VIES exchange procedure.

Tax ID type & application path: Entity_Level_Taxation — For the Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL), the statutory TIN is the NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal), obtained automatically upon incorporation at the Commercial Registry and verification through the AEAT. For a foreign entity without a permanent establishment in Spain, the procedure is to appoint a fiscal representative (if required), submit Form 036 (Censo de Empresarios/Profesionales) or Form 037, together with a power-of-attorney and identity documents, to the competent AEAT office, following which the entity is assigned a provisional NIF-IVA (VAT registration number) or definitively registered as a taxable person. The application must be made prior to the commencement of any taxable activity in Spain; for EU entities, the NIF-IVA may also be sought through the VIES exchange procedure.

Default Tax Classification & Elections

Default tax classification

Entity_Level_Taxation

Available election forms

Spain does not operate a US-style check-the-box or general hybrid-mismatch election. The SL is mandatorily subject to entity-level corporate income tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) at a general rate of 25% (reduced rates apply to newly created entities: 15% for two tax periods and for certain small enterprises). Elective mechanisms available under Spanish tax law include: (i) election for the VAT cash-basis regime (criterio de caja) for small and medium-sized enterprises; (ii) election for group VAT registration under the Special Group VAT Regime (régimen especial de grupo de IVA); (iii) election for a reduced tax-incentive regime for qualifying newly created entities; and (iv) election for consolidated corporate tax grouping under the Spanish consolidated tax group regime. No pass-through election is available for an SL.

VAT / GST & 0% Export Zero-Rating

Standard VAT / GST rate

21%

Mandatory registration threshold (Nexus)

EUR 0 - no general statutory turnover threshold for VAT registration; any taxable person undertaking business activities in Spain must register before commencement. For intra-EU distance sales of goods and to-whom supply of electronically supplied services to non-taxable persons, Spain applies the EU-wide EUR 10,000 calendar-year registration threshold across the EU (unless optional taxability in Spain is elected). For wholesale/re-invoicing trade, registration is compulsory upon the first taxable supply or acquisition of goods in Spain.

Export 0% zero-rating conditions

Exports of goods from Spain to any destination outside the EU are automatically zero-rated (exempt with entitlement to deduction) provided the physical export is completed and evidenced. Zero-rating also applies to intra-EU supplies to VAT-registered customers (with the recipient's valid EU VAT number and EC-sales list reporting), and to certain B2B services supplied to taxable persons established outside the EU (place of supply in the customer's jurisdiction) and services directly related to exported goods, such as loading, transport, and handling, when attributable to the export. For a commercial re-invoicing hub under ISIC 4690, zero-rating is available only when the goods are physically dispatched from Spanish territory; tripartite or chain transactions must be documented to satisfy EU simplified rules (Article 141 of the VAT Directive) or to demonstrate that the first supplier physically exports the goods; otherwise, local 21% VAT applies.

  • Customs Export Declaration (DUA - Documento Único Administrativo)
  • Bill of Lading or Air Waybill or CMR (road transport) evidencing dispatch from Spanish/EU territory
  • Inward Remittance Certificate (bank or payment service provider proof of foreign currency inflow demonstrating export settlement)
  • Commercial invoice and packing list
  • Proof of owner's identity and customs representation authorization (if applicable)
  • EC Sales List (when intra-EU zero-rated supply is claimed)

Spain mandates B2B electronic invoicing in compliance with the Ley Crea y Crece (Law 18/2022) for all entrepreneurs and professionals, with phased implementation after the regulatory development of VeriFactu (fiscal custody system) by AEAT. Large enterprises (annual turnover exceeding EUR 6,010,121.20) must file real-time VAT ledger data through the Suministro Inmediato de Información (SII) system using XML/API submission for each invoice; all businesses will be required to issue e-invoices with VeriFactu's QR-code digital stamping and custody, and clearance through AEAT-approved software. Non-resident VAT-registered entities are equally required to preserve and submit SII records when their turnover exceeds the threshold. Triangular and re-invoicing transactions must also comply with the EU OSS/IOSS procedures where applicable.

AEAT strictly audits zero-rating claims by cross-checking customs export data, transport documents, bank records, and VAT returns. Fraudulent or inaccurate zero-rating claims trigger: (i) a tax assessment with retroactive clawback of the unpaid VAT for up to four years from the assessment deadline, plus statutory late interest; (ii) penalty surcharges ranging from 50% to 100% of the unpaid VAT amount depending on the degree of concealment and cooperation; (iii) if the amount defrauded exceeds EUR 120,000 in one tax period, criminal tax fraud liability under Article 305 of the Código Penal may be imposed, with penalties including imprisonment between two and six years as well as fines; and (iv) loss of entitlement to export zero-rating, exclusion from AEAT's trusted-trader programs, and potential administrative closure during repeated non-compliance.

Stage 04

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

Spain, as a euro-area member, maintains full convertibility for both capital and current account transactions under the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. There are no residual exchange controls on the settlement of trade, repatriation of dividends, or liquidation proceeds for EU/EEA or third-country investors, subject to standard tax withholding and AML reporting. Dividends and profit remittances may be freely transferred once the SL has settled corporate tax (IS) and applicable withholding taxes; treaty-reduced rates may apply upon submission of Spanish tax forms (e.g., Form 210/216/240). Foreign direct investment from non-EU sources may require ex-post declaration to the Foreign Investment Registry, and investments in sectors critical to public security are subject to prior screening under Royal Decree-Law 11/2020. Balance-of-payments reporting obligations to Banco de España arise for any conversion or cross-border transfer exceeding €10,000 per operation.

Export proceeds surrender rules

Spain imposes no statutory surrender, mandatory exchange conversion, or restrictive repatriation timeline for export proceeds. Exporters may hold invoiced foreign currency in domestic or authorised non-resident accounts without a forced conversion to EUR. However, all export and import transactions must be supported by the Single Administrative Document (SAD/EXA) filed with the Spanish Tax Agency (AEAT) for customs and statistical purposes. Cross-border payment receipts and outflows must be declared to Banco de España via the Statistical Declaration of Operations (Form T1/T3) at or above the €10,000 threshold; failure to submit carries administrative penalties. Receipts related to re-invoicing activities should reference the underlying commercial invoices and the applicable ISIC/NACE code to avoid being categorised as financial flows.

Central bank supervision: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), acting within the European System of Central Banks; complementary authority for foreign investment and exchange reporting is exercised by the Secretariat of State for Commerce (Secretaría de Estado de Comercio) through the Foreign Investment Registry (Registro de Inversiones Exteriores).

Offshore Digital Bank / EMI Whitelist

Cross-border EMI / Fintech rails Fit: High

Offshore digital EMIs (Electronic Money Institutions) are viable for the SL only if they hold a valid EU/EEA EMI licence and are registered with the Bank of Spain for cross-border provision of payment services under the Payment Services Directive (PSD2) or Article 5 of Royal Decree-Law 19/2018. An offshore non-EU EMI without a passporting licence is not acceptable for treasury operations. Feasibility rating: Medium-High for an EU-licensed EMI (e.g., operating from Lithuania or Germany) that supports multi-currency IBANs and SWIFT/SEPA; Legal constraints include: (i) the obligation to maintain a Spanish bank account for corporate income tax and VAT filings (AEAT requires a domestic EUR account or a designated agent), (ii) banks may reject deposits from an unregistered EMI, (iii) enhanced AML due diligence is triggered by trade intermediary flows, and (iv) the EMI cannot provide credit facilities or cash-custody services beyond e-money limits.

Core KYC Rejection Triggers & Defense Dossier

Newly formed SL with immediate high-volume cross-border wiring activity and no local physical warehouse or inventory, creating a perceived pass-through risk.

Root cause: Newly formed SL with immediate high-volume cross-border wiring activity and no local physical warehouse or inventory, creating a perceived pass-through risk.

Defense evidence: Notarised deed of incorporation (escritura de constitución); audited or management-prepared business plan; proof of registered office and operational premises (lease agreement, utility invoices); group organisational chart and ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) declaration; signed master framework agreements with related-party suppliers and buyers; historic/forwarding trade flow reconciliation with commercial invoices and purchase orders; and a written compliance memorandum demonstrating that the SL performs genuine re-invoicing and assumes inventory/credit risk.
Payments to or receipts from FATF-grey-listed or high-risk third-country jurisdictions (e.g., certain South American or Middle Eastern states) lacking transparent end-beneficiary information.

Root cause: Payments to or receipts from FATF-grey-listed or high-risk third-country jurisdictions (e.g., certain South American or Middle Eastern states) lacking transparent end-beneficiary information.

Defense evidence: Complete trade documentation pack per transaction, including commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading/airway bill, and customs declaration (SAD); full sanctions and PEP screening results against UN/EU/OFAC lists; correspondent-bank account details with regulatory references; a tailored country risk assessment and AML analysis of the counterparty; end-beneficiary affidavits from the overseas purchasing entity; and a copy of the commercial contract term sheet with payment milestones.
Disproportionate frequency of FX conversions or stated reliance on cash-equivalent instruments (e.g., e-wallets, prepaid cards, or cryptocurrency) contradicting the declared trade intermediary business.

Root cause: Disproportionate frequency of FX conversions or stated reliance on cash-equivalent instruments (e.g., e-wallets, prepaid cards, or cryptocurrency) contradicting the declared trade intermediary business.

Defense evidence: A detailed source-of-wealth and funds report compiling the SL's full current-account statements, complete ledger of receivable/payable invoices, payment gateway settlement reports, and tax filings; notarised declarations from each material counterparty verifying trade purpose; documentary evidence of any third-party funding (shareholder loan agreements or debenture); and, on request, a forensic accountant's assurance opinion on the economic substance and legality of the FX transactions.

Cross-Border Clearing Corridors & Settlement Fit

Compliant inbound capital injections to the Spanish SL must be executed via wire transfer (MT103) or SEPA Credit Transfer in EUR, with the sending party strictly matching the registered shareholder's legal name and domicile. The bank requires a notarised capital-increase deed (escritura de aumento de capital) or a shareholder loan agreement, evidenced by a signed Board resolution and loan terms. The transfer must reference a clear purpose code (e.g., 'FDI-EQUITY' or 'Loan/Shareholder Advance') for the Banco de España statistical declaration; on receipt, Treasury must file Form T1/T3 and, when applicable, the ex-post foreign investment declaration. If the contribution exceeds €3,005,065.08 from a non-EU investor, a prior authorisation may be necessary for sectors subject to Royal Decree-Law 11/2020; for general re-invoicing (NACE 4690) prior authorisation is not automatic but should be screened with the Foreign Investment Registry. No minimum capital escrow is statutorily required for an SL, though the bank may internally require a minimum deposit (often €3,000–€6,000) to activate the relationship.Outbound trade disbursements for the re-invoicing hub will be cleared through three principal rails: (1) SEPA/SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for EUR disbursements to EU/EEA beneficiaries up to the SEPA transaction limit; (2) SWIFT MT103/103+ for non-EEA wired payments, with TARGET2 clearing for euro legs and correspondent-banking for USD/GBP/CNH legs; and (3) Commercial Letters of Credit (documentary credits) for transactional or high-value settlements (typically above €200,000) in higher-risk geographies. Each disbursement instruction must attach the relevant trade documents, customs reference (if applicable), and a statement of beneficial ownership; for jurisdictions with local currency controls, the underlying contract and a valid purpose code (e.g., 'Trade in Goods') must be filed with the paying bank. The treasury system must maintain an immutable payment record, including exchange-rate quotation and SWIFT UETR tracking.EUR/USD Outright Forward Contracts (single-date forwards) with maturities up to 18 months, conducted under an ISDA Master Agreement or the Spanish Master Agreement for Financial Transactions (Acuerdo Marco Español), with a Banco de España-supervised counterparty.Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for currencies subject to capital controls (e.g., Argentine peso, South African rand) through the interbank market, executed only with authorised credit institutions and documented via a nontransferable NDF schedule.Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swaps (CCIRS) for hedging the currency risk and interest rate basis on shareholder loans (e.g., EURIBOR vs. USD SOFR), allowing the SL to convert entire cash-flow streams into a single functional currency.Spot FX facilities allowing same-day settlement and monetisation of export receivables; although not strictly hedging, these are essential liquidity tools.Option-based collars or purchased FX options (costless collar structure) for uncertain re-invoicing flows in volatile emerging-markets currencies, subject to bank credit approval and the suitability assessment under MiFID II.

E-commerce / gateway settlement fit: Offshore digital EMIs (Electronic Money Institutions) are viable for the SL only if they hold a valid EU/EEA EMI licence and are registered with the Bank of Spain for cross-border provision of payment services under the Payment Services Directive (PSD2) or Article 5 of Royal Decree-Law 19/2018. An offshore non-EU EMI without a passporting licence is not acceptable for treasury operations. Feasibility rating: Medium-High for an EU-licensed EMI (e.g., operating from Lithuania or Germany) that supports multi-currency IBANs and SWIFT/SEPA; Legal constraints include: (i) the obligation to maintain a Spanish bank account for corporate income tax and VAT filings (AEAT requires a domestic EUR account or a designated agent), (ii) banks may reject deposits from an unregistered EMI, (iii) enhanced AML due diligence is triggered by trade intermediary flows, and (iv) the EMI cannot provide credit facilities or cash-custody services beyond e-money limits.

Strike-off trigger

Mandatory Audit Threshold Mandatory Audit for All Entities

Turnover: An independent statutory audit is generally mandatory when the company exceeds at least two of these three thresholds for two consecutive financial years: total assets of EUR 2.85 million, annual net turnover of EUR 5.7 million, or average workforce of more than 50 employees. Audit requirements also apply in specified regulated, public-interest, group, or other statutory circumstances.

Mandatory Return Breakdown

Deadline: · Frequency:

Within 25 days following the 6 months after the fiscal year-end (i.e., for calendar year-end, by July 25).

Deadline: · Frequency:

Within the first 20 days of the month following the end of each quarter (April 20, July 20, October 20).

Box-by-Box Return Breakdown (non-resident focus)

BoxField Non-resident guidanceTax-evasion pitfall
Box 1 Tax identification number (NIF) and entity details. Non-resident entities must have a Spanish NIF and file via a tax representative if they have a permanent establishment. Late filing penalty of 5% of the tax amount if filed within 3 months of the deadline, increasing to 20% after 12 months, plus daily surcharge of 1% per month. Fixed penalty of €200 for late filing without tax due.
Box 2 Net accounting result (profit or loss) before adjustments. Report the accounting result as per Spanish GAAP, adjusted for any permanent establishment income. Late filing penalty of 5% of the tax amount if filed within 3 months of the deadline, increasing to 20% after 12 months, plus daily surcharge of 1% per month. Fixed penalty of €200 for late filing without tax due.
Box 3 Adjustments to the accounting result (e.g., permanent differences, temporary differences). Include all required adjustments, including transfer pricing adjustments and disallowed expenses. Late filing penalty of 5% of the tax amount if filed within 3 months of the deadline, increasing to 20% after 12 months, plus daily surcharge of 1% per month. Fixed penalty of €200 for late filing without tax due.
Box 4 Taxable base (after offsetting tax loss carryforwards). Apply any available tax loss carryforwards; Spain allows indefinite carryforward. Late filing penalty of 5% of the tax amount if filed within 3 months of the deadline, increasing to 20% after 12 months, plus daily surcharge of 1% per month. Fixed penalty of €200 for late filing without tax due.
Box 5 Applicable tax rate (standard 25% or reduced 15% for new entities). Use the standard rate unless the entity qualifies for the reduced rate. Late filing penalty of 5% of the tax amount if filed within 3 months of the deadline, increasing to 20% after 12 months, plus daily surcharge of 1% per month. Fixed penalty of €200 for late filing without tax due.
Box 6 Gross tax liability before deductions and credits. Calculate based on taxable base and rate. Late filing penalty of 5% of the tax amount if filed within 3 months of the deadline, increasing to 20% after 12 months, plus daily surcharge of 1% per month. Fixed penalty of €200 for late filing without tax due.
Box 7 Deductions and tax credits (e.g., double taxation relief, R&D credits). Claim treaty relief for foreign taxes paid, if applicable. Late filing penalty of 5% of the tax amount if filed within 3 months of the deadline, increasing to 20% after 12 months, plus daily surcharge of 1% per month. Fixed penalty of €200 for late filing without tax due.
Box 8 Final tax payable or refund due. Ensure all prepayments (Modelo 202) are credited. Late filing penalty of 5% of the tax amount if filed within 3 months of the deadline, increasing to 20% after 12 months, plus daily surcharge of 1% per month. Fixed penalty of €200 for late filing without tax due.
Box 1 Tax period (quarter and fiscal year). Non-resident entities with a permanent establishment must file; others are not required. Late filing penalty of 5% of the prepayment amount, plus daily surcharge of 1% per month, and fixed penalty of €200 if no amount due.
Box 2 Estimated taxable base for the quarter (based on prior year's tax or actual results). Use the method chosen (e.g., 18% of prior year's taxable base). Late filing penalty of 5% of the prepayment amount, plus daily surcharge of 1% per month, and fixed penalty of €200 if no amount due.
Box 3 Prepayment amount (tax rate applied to estimated base). Apply the standard 25% rate unless reduced rate applies. Late filing penalty of 5% of the prepayment amount, plus daily surcharge of 1% per month, and fixed penalty of €200 if no amount due.

Transfer Pricing & Economic Substance

Master / Local File threshold: Entities with net revenue exceeding €10 million must prepare Local File and Master File. Below this threshold, a simplified documentation (summary) is required.

Economic substance scope: Spain applies substance-over-form principles. While there is no specific ESR, the General Anti-Abuse Rule (GAAR) and CFC rules require that entities have real economic substance (staff, premises, functions) to justify recharacterization. For re-invoicing hubs, substance is critical to avoid being treated as a shell company.

Fatal Compliance Red Lines & Director Liability

Tax Evasion

Statutory sanction: Penalty of 50% to 150% of the tax evaded, plus administrative interest. Criminal prosecution for amounts exceeding €50,000 per year.

Director personal liability: Directors can be held personally liable for civil restitution, travel bans, and imprisonment up to 6 years for tax evasion.
Shell Company / Artificial Arrangement

Statutory sanction: Recharacterization of transactions, disallowance of deductions, application of CFC rules, and penalty of 50% of the tax avoided.

Director personal liability: Directors may face personal liability for unpaid taxes and penalties, and criminal charges for fraud.
Anti-Money Laundering (AML) Violation

Statutory sanction: Fines up to €1 million or 1% of annual turnover, and suspension of business activity.

Director personal liability: Directors can be personally fined and banned from managing companies for up to 10 years.
